claims.statement: The row chart counts rows, orders by count across all rows, and sizes Other from chart height. Vertical bars read a grouped summary through aggregateId, order by data or label only, and have no Other. Saved-data validation accepts aggregateId on any chart type. summarizeGroup can pool any set of rows under a summary spec.

claims.statement: The row chart is the horizontal home; vertical bars gain no orientation switch.
The measure is a named grouped summary reusable by other charts, not a private per-chart setting.
When other charts filter, order and Other membership hold; filtered values draw over unfiltered context.
An explicit saved Top N fixes Other membership across resizes; unset keeps today's fit-to-height.
Signed measures draw on both sides of a zero line in the first release.
The ranking is writable and round-trips in dashboard text in the first release.
Composition-mode horizontal measure rows and a 'show as rows' switch from a vertical bar are later.
claims.notes: Not selected for the first release on 2026-10-10.

themes: Rank count, sum, or average from a named grouped summary in the row chart.

shape.appetite: One row-chart renderer extension plus settings, dashboard-text keys, and tests. No new chart type and no shared bar framework.
shape.problem: The row chart can only count, so a horizontal ranking of revenue silently becomes a ranking of records, and its Other membership shifts on resize.
shape.recommended_shape: Row chart gains an optional aggregateId and topN. It reads the same getAggregateResult output as vertical bars for live rows and for all rows; order comes from all rows, filtered values draw over unfiltered context, Other is pooled with summarizeGroup over its members' rows, and the x domain spans zero for signed values. Count mode (no aggregateId) keeps today's behavior: per-row counts, order by all-row count, fit-to-height Other. Only an explicit topN changes it.
shape.simpler_counterproposal: Add aggregateId and draw live values only, keeping height-driven Other and re-ranking on every filter. Rejected: the user chose a held order and fixed membership, and averaging bar values for Other would drift from vertical bars.
success_moves: Consume the existing AggregateResult instead of a second aggregation path, so both orientations agree by construction.
Pool Other through summarizeGroup over member rows, so averages and once-per IDs stay correct.
Make topN optional with unset meaning today's fit-to-height, so saved row charts render unchanged.
Prove on two existing demo summaries (shop sum, Beijing signed average) with vertical twins as oracles.
Keep removal trivial: unsetting aggregateId returns the chart to counting.

first_proof.question: Can the row chart render a grouped summary, pooled Other, and held order from the existing summary result plus one pooling call, matching vertical bars?
first_proof.artifact: Shop revenue-by-region and Beijing above-reference row rankings beside their vertical bars in the demo, plus planner fixture tests.
first_proof.try: Shop row ranking on revenue-by-region beside its vertical bar, filter by Category; Beijing row ranking on above-reference with topN=5.
first_proof.observe: Values match vertical bars and a hand total; negatives left of zero; Other's average equals pooled average; order and membership hold through filtering and resize; Alt-click lists correct contributors.
first_proof.decide: If the existing summary result plus one pooling call suffices, build the rest on it; otherwise extract a shared ranking plan first.
first_proof.decision_rule: If the existing summary result plus one pooling call suffices, build the rest on it; otherwise extract a shared ranking plan first.

rabbit_holes: Average context drawn as a faint bar can sit shorter than the filtered value; evaluate a tick.
Top N at very small heights: rows compress rather than change membership; label thinning may be needed.
